should_trigger: Set up who edits what between Claude Code and Cowork on this repository.
Write the HANDOFF.md so the next session can continue.
I want to change the README but Cowork owns it; propose the change.
Give me paste-ready project instructions for the Cowork project.
Which agent should commit published files?
should_not_trigger: Build a knowledge pack for the engagement closure.
Assign Jira tickets to the team.
Write a RACI for the project.
Export this chat so I can continue elsewhere.
Write the changelog entry for architecture 0.4.0.
Summarize today's session in a message to the team.
Write a resume file that carries the open items across engagements, with the knowledge pack.

evals.prompt: Write the 'Who writes what' section and a HANDOFF.md for the fixture repository, assuming one shell-capable agent and one rendering agent.
evals.expected_output: A 'Who writes what' section with one writing agent per path, an observed-capabilities table, and an untracked HANDOFF.md in the house template.
assertions: Gives a table in which every path has exactly one writing agent; no path lists two
Assigns arc42/, CHANGELOG.md, README.md and tools/ to the shell-capable agent and briefs/ and generated/ to the rendering agent
Splits published/ between the agent that builds and the agent that commits
Includes a capabilities table written as observed on this repository, with Can and Cannot columns for each agent
States that a change to a file the agent does not own arrives as a proposal block and that handoffs do not become files
HANDOFF.md carries uncommitted changes with a ready commit message, open decisions with owners, next work in order and state checks, and is stated to be git-ignored and overwritten at each handoff

evals.prompt: Claude Code has just bumped the fixture architecture to 0.4.0 after registering a seventh component. README.md still says 'Architecture 0.3.1 · Estimate 0.2.0'. You are the Cowork session. Get the README right.
evals.expected_output: A proposal block addressed to the README's owner, not an edit of the file.
assertions: Does not edit README.md and does not claim to have changed it
Produces a proposal block naming the file, an anchor, a replacement, a reason and what the change obligates
The anchor is the exact current text (the versions line or 'Architecture 0.3.1') and the replacement carries 0.4.0
The obligations include the changelog entry and a review of the estimate's pin, since a MINOR below 1.0.0 breaks the pin
Names the owning agent (shell and git) as the one who applies the block, runs the audit and commits
